analysis_steps.goal: Measure stellar continuum radius and brightness

method.value: Measure I_star at disk center and equivalent uniform-disk R_star from integrated continuum flux in spw2 continuum image

evidence.quote: we estimate $R_\mathrm{star}$ from the integrated continuum flux $I(r,\theta)$ and the surface brightness measured at the center of the disk $I_\mathrm{star}$

analysis_steps.goal: Determine line profile and systemic velocity

method.value: Gaussian profile from absorption at disk center and emission ring; emission velocity adopted as systemic

evidence.quote: We adopted the emission line velocity as the systemic velocity $\varv_\mathrm{sys}$

analysis_steps.goal: Fit thin shell model to radial profile

method.value: R_shell from peak of azimuthally averaged radial profile; fit I_shell*tau_shell and tau_cool with beam-convolved model

evidence.quote: The model profile is adjusted to the ALMA radial intensity profile $I(r)$ (Fig. [7](#radprofiles)), using as variables $I_\mathrm{shell}\,\tau_\mathrm{shell}$ and the optical depth of the cooler absorbing layer
We make the assumption here that the light-emitting layer is optically thin ($\tau_\mathrm{shell} \ll 1$)
we used a classical Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm based on the SciPy routine `scipy.optimize.leastsq`

validation.value: A thick-shell fit was attempted but was unstable

evidence.quote: We attempted to fit a thick shell model, adding one parameter in the model (the shell thickness), but the results are unstable

method.value: Compensate absorption in the cube, then fit Gaussian (amplitude, width, velocity) per position

evidence.quote: At each position of the absorption compensated data cube, we fit a Gaussian profile on the emission line with three parameters

method.value: Fit solid body rotation (v_sys, v_eq sin i, PA), with and without expansion term, to velocity map within stellar disk

evidence.quote: The three model parameters are the systemic velocity $\varv_\mathrm{sys}$ in the local standard of rest (LSR), the projected rotation velocity $\varv_\mathrm{eq}\,\sin i$, and the position angle of the polar axis $PA$.

key_parameters.value: v_sys fixed to emission ring value; fit radius varied by ±15% for systematics

evidence.quote: we chose the approach to modulate the radius over which the fit is computed by $\pm 15\%$ around the continuum radius of the star
This simple model assumes that the angular rotation velocity is independent of latitude.

fitting.value: chi2 fit; uncertainties scaled by sqrt(chi2_red)

evidence.quote: The listed uncertainties of the model parameters have been scaled by $(\chi^2_\mathrm{red})^{1/2}$

validation.value: Compared four lines; differential rotation fit gave no significant improvement

evidence.quote: the adjustment of this model does not bring a significant improvement of the $\chi^2$ or residuals of the fit

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular shell co-rotates with star; no significant global outflow at 40 mas; hot spot, plume and dust arc aligned with polar axis, suggesting focused mass loss from a rogue convection cell

evidence.quote: suggests that focused mass loss is currently taking place in the polar region of the star.

claims.hypothesis: Betelgeuse's rotation can be measured from ALMA SiO velocity map
claims.experiment: Solid body rotation fit to SiO v=2 J=8-7 emission velocity map
claims.result: v_eq sin i = 5.47 ± 0.25 km/s, PA = 48.0 ± 3.5 deg
claims.finding: Betelgeuse rotates slowly with P/sin i = 36 ± 8 yr

evidence.quote: we show that the supergiant is rotating with a projected equatorial velocity of $\varv_\mathrm{eq}\sin i = 5.47\pm 0.25$ km s$^{-1}$

claims.hypothesis: The chromosphere co-rotates with the star
claims.experiment: Compare ALMA velocity with UV measurements at larger radii
claims.result: Linear velocities similar, angular velocity lower at larger radii

evidence.quote: the chromosphere is co-rotating with the star up to a radius of $\approx 10$ au

claims.hypothesis: Hot spot, plume and dust shell reveal focused mass loss from rogue convection cells
claims.experiment: Compare PA of pole, ALMA hot spot, molecular plume, and dust arc
claims.finding: Focused mass loss from rogue cell; scenario not directly confirmed

evidence.quote: We propose that this hot spot corresponds to the location of a particularly strong “rogue” convection cell

why_this_method.value: SiO v=2 line chosen as best match to thin shell model and likely traces regions closest to star

evidence.quote: We chose this line as its intensity profile is the best match to our thin shell model

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Thick shell model unstable; differential rotation model gave no significant improvement

evidence.quote: We attempted to fit a thick shell model, adding one parameter in the model (the shell thickness), but the results are unstable

limitations_admitted.value: Inclination cannot be determined; resolution insufficient for differential rotation

evidence.quote: For this reason, we cannot conclude firmly on the inclination of the polar axis on the line of sight.

referee_caveats_inferred: Rotation signal could be mimicked by non-radial pulsation or turbulence; only ~4 resolution elements across disk
Simple thin-shell model with fixed parameters; no joint fit or MCMC
